title: Authority ledger migration and SSO attribute reconciliation runbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Migrate the current role/permission ledger (RBAC v1) to the new Authority Ledger (RBAC v2) with three coordinated streams: dual-write compatibility layer, incremental backfill + reconciliation, and SSO/SAML attribute mapping reconciliation. The goal is a low-risk migration that preserves audit history, minimizes auth failures during cutover, and provides clear rollback paths. This ticket captures runbook steps, gating checks, observability signals, customer comms, and post-cutover validation checks.
background_and_goals: Background: RBAC v1 stores role assignments and permission grants in a monolithic table with denormalized blobs. RBAC v2 introduces a normalized authority ledger, versioned role artifacts, and audit-forwarding to the centralized audit pipeline. Goals: 1) Ensure no data loss of role grants and audit events; 2) Keep production auth failures under 0.05% during migration; 3) Provide per-organization canaries and an automated rollback runway; 4) Reconcile SSO/SAML attribute mappings with new role identifiers.
non_goals_and_constraints: Non-goals: full UI redesign of the Admin Console (out of scope for this migration). Constraints: database writes must avoid table locks >30s; customer-facing downtime is unacceptable; migration workers must respect rate limits on downstream identity providers (IdPs).
decision_log: Decisions made: 1) Use dual-write shim (rbac-compat service) instead of big-bang snapshot to allow gradual cutover; 2) Keep v1 read path until a 2-week observation window after cutover; 3) Audit events will be forwarded to the existing audit pipeline with an added v2_metadata field; 4) Implement SAML attribute reconciliation as a separate pre-cutover job to avoid coupling with backfill.
tradeoffs: Trade-offs considered: - Dual-write increases write path complexity and surface area for bugs, but minimizes customer impact and provides easier rollback. - Big-bang export/import would be simpler code-wise but causes application-level consistency risks and long maintenance windows. - Immediate v1 deprecation reduces maintenance burden but is higher risk for customers using custom SAML mappings.
migration_strategy_overview: Phased approach: Phase 0: Prep and entitlement mapping verification. Phase 1: Enable dual-write in shadow mode and run continuous reconciliation jobs. Phase 2: Backfill historical role grants (rate-limited workers) and run full reconciliation. Phase 3: Per-org canary cutovers by org size and tier. Phase 4: Global cutover with v1 read-only, monitoring, and rollback gates. Phase 5: Deprecation and cleanup after observation window.
detailed_runbook_steps: Prep: - Freeze schema changes for two weeks before cutover. - Run discovery job to enumerate SSO mappings and orphaned roles. - Notify customers with custom mappings (see customer_comms_draft). Dual-write: - Deploy rbac-compat with feature flag 'dual_write_v2' default=false. - Start in shadow mode (writes to v2 but not used by auth decision), log diffs to GitHub PR and Sentry. - Enable reconciliation scorer that computes 'role_mismatch_rate'. Backfill: - Start backfill workers by region, prioritized by last-active orgs. - Use exponential backoff and token-bucket rate limiting to avoid spamming IdPs. - Keep per-org progress in migration_progress table. Canary cutover: - Select 5 orgs by tier (1 small, 2 mid, 2 large) and schedule a 2-hour window. - Enable 'auth_read_v2' for org, run smoke tests, validate authz success rate <0.05% error. Global cutover: - Open 30-minute maintenance window in internal ops; set v1 to read-only; flip 'auth_read_v2' globally; monitor; if errors exceed threshold, rollback to v1 read path and the dual-write shim remains in place for diagnostics.
observability_and_metrics: Primary metrics: - authz_success_rate (target >= 99.95%) - role_mismatch_rate (target < 0.1%) - audit_event_delivery_latency (p50/p95/p99) - dual_write_diff_rate (percentage of writes that disagree) Dashboards: link: https://dashboards.internal.redwood/infrastructure/rbac_migration (placeholder). Alerts: - SEV-1 if authz_success_rate drops below 99% for >5m. - SEV-2 if dual_write_diff_rate > 1% for >10m.
reconciliation_and_backfill: Reconciliation algorithm: - For each org, join v1_role_grants to v2_authority_entries on user_email + resource fingerprint. - Compute confidence score using last_updated_ts, binding_count, and SSO mapping hash. - Flag low-confidence mappings for manual review. Backfill plan: - Backfill workers will process historical grants in descending timestamp order. - Continuous reconciler will re-run until daily diff <0.01% for a 24h window.
sso_saml_mapping_plan: SSO risks: SAML attributes may map to role names (not stable IDs) and customers use custom mappings. Steps: 1) Run attribute-mapping discovery job to capture live mappings. 2) Build mapping table that translates SAML attributes to v2 role IDs; include fallbacks to role name fuzzy-match. 3) Provide admin UI to surface unmapped attributes pre-cutover. 4) Offer a one-click suggested mapping per-org in Console. For partners with IdP rate limits, coordinate migration windows.
customer_communication_and_support: Customer comms plan: - T-minus 30d: high-level announcement to admins with timeline and benefits. - T-minus 14d: per-org discovery report showing whether custom SAML mappings exist and suggested actions. - T-minus 7d: scheduled migration window and opt-out instructions for enterprise customers. - During cutover: status in Status Page (https://status.redwood.ai) and dedicated Slack channel #rbac-migration-support. Support playbook: - Escalation matrix, runbook quick-steps (revert to v1 read path, toggle dual_write flag), and contact list for SRE/Identity/PM.
rollback_and_failure_modes: Rollback options: - Soft rollback: set 'auth_read_v2' off globally and keep dual-write enabled to collect postmortem diffs. - Hard rollback: revert database writes from v2 where possible (requires running compensating deletes) — only if soft rollback cannot contain errors. Failure modes and mitigations: - Higher authz failure rate: invoke soft rollback, open SEV channel, notify customers. - Missing audit events: re-run audit-forwarding from v1 event horizon logs; notify Compliance.
validation_and_post_cutover_checks: Post-cutover checklist: - No increase in auth latency >5% p95. - Audit event parity >= 99.9% for the last 7 days. - No open unmapped SSO attributes for top 100 orgs. - Dual_write_diff_rate < 0.01% consistently for 7 days. - Security review signoff and compliance signoff logged in Confluence.
